frozen_hypothesis.hypothesis: For the 3-Chloropyridine Suzuki target, source evidence from the same substrate will transfer such that P2L1 XPhos Cl candidates in the high-temperature, high-precatalyst-fraction region are most likely to give the best initial yields, with long residence time helping but being less important than temperature.
frozen_hypothesis.mechanism: The completed same-substrate source shows the strongest positive outcome correlation with normalized feature 0 (0.601612), consistent with temperature being the dominant transferable driver. It also shows P2L1 XPhos Cl is a credible high-performing chemistry family on this substrate (mean 61.11, max 82.91), so focusing initial picks inside that group reduces negative transfer risk versus unconstrained diversity. Candidate 024 is the best source-supported P2L1 quality anchor because it combines maximal temperature, long residence time, and near-maximal precatalyst fraction. Candidate 059 preserves high residence time and high loading but drops temperature, testing whether the strong temperature trend transfers. Candidate 057 keeps very high temperature and high loading but shortens residence time, testing whether residence time is secondary once temperature and loading are favorable.
failure_conditions: If the new target reverses the source temperature trend, so high temperature is not beneficial for P2L1 XPhos Cl.
If residence time is actually the dominant driver in the target and short-time high-temperature conditions underperform strongly.
If cross-campaign effects make P2L1 XPhos Cl behave qualitatively differently from its same-substrate source summary.
If an untested low-loading or lower-temperature regime unexpectedly dominates, indicating source-to-target transfer is weak in this campaign.

frozen_reflection.evidence_interpretation: The revealed results show that candidate 024 from the P2L1 XPhos Cl group performed well (85.4755), supporting the hypothesis that high temperature and high precatalyst fraction are beneficial. However, candidate 039 from the P1L1 XPhos OMs group also performed well (80.6121) under slightly lower temperature and higher residence time, suggesting that the temperature trend may not be as dominant as initially thought. This indicates a potential contradiction regarding the importance of temperature versus residence time.
frozen_reflection.revised_hypothesis: For the 3-Chloropyridine Suzuki target, source evidence from the same substrate will transfer such that P2L1 XPhos Cl candidates in the high-temperature, high-precatalyst-fraction region are likely to give good initial yields, but residence time may also play a significant role, potentially challenging the dominance of temperature.
frozen_reflection.next_experiment_rationale: Selecting candidates 049 and 042 allows us to test the revised hypothesis against different temperature and residence time conditions. Candidate 049 has a lower temperature but longer residence time, while candidate 042 maintains high temperature and residence time, providing a direct comparison to assess the influence of these factors on yield.
